targetText: If conquest constituted a natural right on the part of the few, the many have only to gather sufficient strength in order to acquire the natural right of reconquering what has been taken from them.
quote: If conquest constituted a natural right on the part of the few, the many have only to gather sufficient strength in order to acquire the natural right of reconquering what has been taken from them.
summary: Private landed property originated in violent conquest, not moral right, and the working class has the right to reclaim it.
explanation: Marx demystifies bourgeois property law: private ownership of natural resources was never created by peaceful contract or moral right, but by violent historical expropriation. The working-class majority holds the historical right to reclaim collective ownership of the earth.

targetText: The imperative wants of society will and must be satisfied, changes dictated by social necessity will work their own way, and sooner or later adapt legislation to their interests.
quote: The imperative wants of society will and must be satisfied, changes dictated by social necessity will work their own way, and sooner or later adapt legislation to their interests.
summary: Productive necessities and social development compel legal superstructures to adapt to modern economic requirements.
explanation: Historical materialist principle: economic forces and productive necessities ultimately determine legal superstructures. As population growth and modern industrial farming require coordinated large-scale resource management, private property laws become obsolete fetters that must give way.

targetText: This form of landed property and the piecemeal cultivation it necessitates, while excluding all appliances of modern agricultural improvements, converts the tiller himself into the most decided enemy to social progress and, above all, the nationalisation of land.
quote: This form of landed property and the piecemeal cultivation it necessitates, while excluding all appliances of modern agricultural improvements, converts the tiller himself into the most decided enemy to social progress and, above all, the nationalisation of land.
summary: Piecemeal peasant proprietorship excludes modern agricultural science and turns small tillers into opponents of social progress.
explanation: Marx identifies the structural contradiction of small peasant proprietorship (as in post-revolutionary France): trapped on small plots and mortgaged to banks, smallholders cling fanatically to nominal private ownership, opposing socialist transformation despite their own extreme poverty.

targetText: To give up the soil to the hands of associated rural labourers, would be to surrender society to one exclusive class of producers.
quote: To give up the soil to the hands of associated rural labourers, would be to surrender society to one exclusive class of producers.
summary: Land must belong to the entire society, not just local agricultural cooperatives, to prevent sectional monopolies.
explanation: Marx refutes syndicalist and guild-socialist ideas of cooperative land parceling: natural resources cannot belong merely to those who happen to work them locally, but must belong to the entire working-class society to prevent sector-specific monopolies and inequalities.

targetText: National centralisation of the means of production will become the national basis of a society composed of associations of free and equal producers, carrying on the social business on a common and rational plan.
quote: National centralisation of the means of production will become the national basis of a society composed of associations of free and equal producers, carrying on the social business on a common and rational plan.
summary: Centralizing the means of production under democratic public ownership provides the basis for common, rational economic planning.
explanation: The definitive Marxist vision of socialist planning: centralizing land, energy, and major industries under democratic public ownership allows society to abolish class exploitation and direct production through a coordinated, rational social plan.
